message.content: The sea usually looks **blue**—that’s because water absorbs longer wavelengths (red, orange, yellow) and scatters the shorter blue wavelengths back to our eyes. In shallow or clear water it can appear turquoise or teal, while in deeper or murkier conditions it may look greenish or even dark gray. Algae, sediment, and the angle of the sun can all shift the perceived hue, so the “color” of the sea is actually a mix of many factors rather than a single fixed shade.
